summary:
Two test-only fixes, no production change.

1) tests/idma_batch_start_harness.c, writeq() config-write guard: the assertion used the global CPU interrupt state `!irq_disabled_depth`, but production `idma_batch_start()` performs the submission-configuration writes *outside* its own protected trigger window (idma.c:512-517), so a caller that already enters with global IRQs disabled (the `irq_restore_paths` (c) fixture sets `irq_disabled_depth = 1`) must be allowed. The guard now checks only the driver's own window depth (`!driver_irq_depth`) plus preemption (`!preempt_disabled_depth`); the NEXT_ID trigger read assert (`irq_disabled_depth && preempt_disabled_depth`, harness line 150) is unchanged, so the IRQ-restoration/no-IRQ-taken assertions of that case stay meaningful and the case is not removed. This matches the driver invariant: configuration outside the OWN critical region, only the A-then-V trigger reads inside it.

2) tests/idma_scheduler_harness.c, diag-branch cross-lane ordering check (line 618): the old assertion `lane[1].launch_end_ns < lane[0].launch_begin_ns` encoded the previous per-lane sequential config/trigger order. After the batch-start change both register sets are configured before either NEXT_ID trigger (idma.c:512-517 then 537-566), so the stamped order is necessarily A-config-begin (lane[1].launch_begin) < V-config-begin (lane[0].launch_begin) < A-trigger-end (lane[1].launch_end) < V-trigger-end (lane[0].launch_end); the two launch brackets now overlap. The check is replaced by the real ordering: both configuration begins before the first trigger end, and A's trigger end before V's trigger end. `launch_begin_ns` still records the configuration-write begin instant (field name kept for ABI compatibility; production timestamps unchanged), noted in a comment. The solo branch assertion is preserved, the per-lane loop check at line 613 (`l->launch_begin_ns > g->arm_end_ns && l->launch_end_ns > l->launch_begin_ns`) is untouched, and every other diag check (rounds, warm/arm stamps, offsets, HPM counters, submit counts) is preserved. All five cases failing at scheduler.c:2042 in the attached log (diag_ok, diag_no_warmup, diag_fast_a, diag_trigger, diag_second_bad) reach the final else branch with both lanes configured and triggered, so the new checks hold there; zero/quarantine paths exit before this branch.

Acceptance checks (to be executed by Codex; worker cannot execute):
- `tests/test_idma_batch_start.py` (case `irq_restore_paths`) exits 0; ASSERTS still show no IRQ serviced while `irq_disabled_depth == 1`.
- `tests/test_idma_scheduler.py` exits 0; previously failing diag cases PASS, all other cases (queue_/pair_/path_/batch_/p4m_/observer_/cache_/verify_/...) unchanged and still pass.

Files intentionally NOT changed: linux/drivers/misc/idma.c.

edits.old:
/*
     * Submission configuration must never be written with IRQs or preemption
     * disabled; only the trigger reads belong to the protected section.
     */
    if (offset == IDMA_SRC_ADDR_REG_OFFSET || offset == IDMA_DST_ADDR_REG_OFFSET ||
        offset == IDMA_NUM_BYTES_REG_OFFSET || offset == IDMA_CONF_REG_OFFSET)
        assert(!irq_disabled_depth && !preempt_disabled_depth);
edits.new:
/*
     * Submission configuration must never be written while this driver still
     * holds its own trigger window or while preemption is disabled; only the
     * trigger reads belong to the protected section.  A caller may already
     * have global IRQs disabled (irq_disabled_depth > 0) when it enters; that
     * is legal here and is what the irq_restore_paths fixture (c) exercises.
     */
    if (offset == IDMA_SRC_ADDR_REG_OFFSET || offset == IDMA_DST_ADDR_REG_OFFSET ||
        offset == IDMA_NUM_BYTES_REG_OFFSET || offset == IDMA_CONF_REG_OFFSET)
        assert(!driver_irq_depth && !preempt_disabled_depth);

risks: The diag-branch replacement assumes that in the final-else cases both lanes actually reached the batch trigger, so lane[1].launch_end_ns (A-trigger end) and lane[0].launch_end_ns (V-trigger end) are non-zero. This holds for the five failing cases in the attached log (diag_ok, diag_no_warmup, diag_fast_a, diag_trigger, diag_second_bad: diag_second_bad fails in idma_e3_finish after a full launch, not in the trigger). Zero-ID/quarantine/timeout/interrupt paths take the earlier `ret && !bad` branch and never reach these asserts; the solo case keeps its own existing assert.

The three new strict `<` comparisons rely on the scheduler harness ktime stub being strictly monotonic (each ktime_get_ns() call advances `now`). If that stub is ever changed to return a coarse/unadvanced timestamp, the comparisons would need `<=`; they are not valid with equal timestamps.

Edit 1 deliberately narrows the config-write guard from global IRQ state to the driver's own window. This is correct for idma_batch_start() (config before preempt_disable()/local_irq_save()), but if a future production change moves a config write inside the driver window the guard (`!driver_irq_depth`) will still catch it, while a caller-IRQ-off configuration remains permitted by design.

Both edits are only proposed; I could not compile or run anything. The parent must run tests/test_idma_batch_start.py and tests/test_idma_scheduler.py to confirm no other assertion (e.g. the untouched order_both MMIO-index checks, or the per-lane loop check at scheduler line 613) regresses.

No production code (linux/drivers/misc/idma.c) is modified; if the parent instead expects the diagnostic field to be renamed or re-stamped, that is out of scope of this request and would break the stated ABI semantics.
